dependency_passages_read.use: Right Ore RMS2 and right cancellation RMS3, with the correct source/target orientation.
Right roofs, equality after refinement, and S/X with arbitrary commuting arrows.
Quasi-isomorphisms form a bilateral multiplicative system in the ambient homotopy category; D(A) is its localization.
Natural N(V) -> s(V) is a quasi-isomorphism.
Maintained one-variable Dold-Kan theorem as dependency only; no review of the candidate's iterated-normalization theorem.
Simplicial homotopies give normalized chain homotopies.

checks.reason: For a small category, finite paths in the graph enlarged by inverse edges form a set. The generated congruence imposes precisely identities, old compositions, and inverse equations. A functor inverting S has a forced extension; naturality across s implies naturality across s-inverse. No Ore assumptions are needed for this first assertion.

The identity is an object. Given s1:X1->X and s2:X2->X in S, RMS2 gives a common predecessor whose composite denominator is in S by closure. Given a,b:X1->X2 over X, s2 a=s2 b; RMS3 provides t in S with a t=b t, and s1 t is again a denominator. Arbitrary commuting arrows, not only arrows in S, are correctly permitted.

For h:X'->X'' in S/X with s''h=s', Q(h)Q(s')^-1=Q(s'')^-1, so the displayed assignment is covariant. Objects of (I_X -> J_X) over (Y,a) are roofs with numerator b and Q(b)Q(s)^-1=a. Existence is right fractions. Use Ore to place two roofs over one denominator, then 04VJ to equalize numerators after further S-refinement. This yields a common predecessor in the comma category, hence connectedness and initiality.

checks.topic: Essentially constant pro-object gives the required limit
checks.reason: For the constant embedding c, Hom_Pro(cB,(F(X')))=lim_{I_X} Hom_B(B,F(X')). A chosen pro-isomorphism cL_X ~= (F(X')) therefore represents this cone functor. This proves existence of the actual limit without assuming arbitrary limits in B or using a reversed pro-Hom formula.

An arrow r:QX->QY sends (Z,a:QY->QZ) in J_Y to (Z,a r) in J_X. Restricting the universal J_X-cone produces a map L_X->L_Y, so LF is covariant. Evaluation at (X,id) gives u_X:L_X->F(X). For eta:GQ->F, components eta_Y G(a) are a J_X-cone; universal factorization gives G(QX)->L_X. Naturality and uniqueness establish Nat(G,LF) ~= Nat(GQ,F), with the stated counit direction.

Taking opposite categories interchanges right/left multiplicative systems, pro/ind objects and limit/colimit constructions. It reverses the counit to F->RF Q. The proof uses only category-theoretic assumptions plus the size convention and essential constancy; no additive, exact, triangulated, injective, or projective hypothesis is silently introduced.

The natural quasi-isomorphism N(X)->s(X) and the commuting naturality square show W_s is exactly detected by N. The existing one-variable Dold-Kan equivalence carries W and W_s both ways; its natural unit and counit descend through localization. Reindexing C^i=C_{-i} converts nonnegative chains to complexes zero in positive cochain degree.

checks.topic: Cylinder, degree bound, and contraction signs
checks.reason: For d_E(a,b)=(da+b,-db), d_E^2=0. With t(a,b)=(0,a), d_E t(a,b)=(a,-da) and t d_E(a,b)=(0,da+b), so d_E t+t d_E=id. j(a)=(a,0) is a chain map. E^n=0 for n>0 when C is nonpositive, although E may extend one degree farther downward, which is allowed. Thus the cylinder stays within the fixed nonpositive bound and p:C+E->C is a homotopy equivalence.

checks.topic: Homotopy extension signs and quotient factorization
checks.reason: Put k=f-g=dh+hd and phi(a,b)=k(a)+h(b). Then d_D phi=k da+d_D h b, while phi d_E=k da+k b-h db=k da+d_D h b. Thus phi is a chain map. Combined with g on the C summand, its restrictions along i0 and i1 are g and g+k=f. Since p i0=p i1=id, inverting homotopy equivalences forces i0=i1 and hence f=g. Conversely quotienting homotopies inverts homotopy equivalences. The two maintained Dold-Kan homotopy lemmas transfer this to simplicial objects.

For cochain homotopy h^n:C^n->D^{n-1}, restrict h^0 to ker d_C^0 and keep lower components. In degree zero, h^1 d_C^0 vanishes on that kernel; in degree -1, d_C^-1 factors through ker d_C^0, so the homotopy equation is preserved at the boundary as well as below it. Hence smart truncation induces a functor K(A)->K^{<=0}(A), fixes nonpositive complexes, and preserves quasi-isomorphisms by its cohomology description.

checks.topic: Both Ore and cancellation calculi at the fixed bound
checks.reason: Start with each ambient Ore or cancellation diagram in K(A), whose existence follows from 05RT. Apply canonical truncation to every object and arrow. Boundary objects already in K^{<=0} are fixed; equalities remain equalities because truncation is functorial on K; required denominators remain quasi-isomorphisms. This supplies both calculi without the false claim that K^{<=0} is triangulated.

For a roof C<-Z->D with C,D nonpositive and left map a quasi-isomorphism, H^{>0}(Z)=0. Consequently tau<=0 Z->Z is a quasi-isomorphism and truncation produces a roof within the fixed-bound homotopy category. An equality between two ambient roofs is witnessed by a common refinement with its total denominator in W; its middle complex likewise has vanishing positive cohomology, so truncation preserves the equality witness. Every derived object with H^{>0}=0 is represented by its canonical nonpositive truncation. This proves exactly the full subcategory D^{<=0}, not all bounded-above objects.
